newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Evergreen increases plantation value.
newsitem.headline: Evergreen increases plantation value.

text.p: Evergreen Forests' plantations increased in value by 24 percent over the six months to December 31 as a result of acquisitions and development, the company said on Monday.

Chief Executive Mark Bogle said that at a discount rate of nine percent, Groome Poyry's valuation of the tree crop at December 31 was NZ$89.9 million against $72.2 million six months earlier, equating to net asset backing of NZ$0.97 per share.
Over the six months, Evergreen's operating deficit after tax was of NZ$195,000, up from $135,000 a year ago on revenue of NZ$695,000.
Revenue had fallen from NZ$1.5 million a year earlier due to a reduction in harvesting on the West Coast of the South Island, as foreshadowed in the annual report.
Harvesting was reduced because the directors believed the net return to shareholders, at present log prices, was lower than could be obtained by allowing the trees to grow.
Until forecast harvesting in 1998/99, operating profits would remain at or slightly below break-even, Bogle said.
In the meantime, Evergreen would continue its strategy of growing by acquisition and planting, Bogle said.
